stages.text: Folk walk in from three villages to see {heroName}, the one in the ballads.

success.text: Ballads and beer.
The hero isn't thrilled.

stories.title: A crowd for an infamous hero

stages.text: A crowd wants {heroName} gone: villages burned, they say, on the hero's last road.

success.text: It was the raiders. The crowd believes you.

failure.text: The crowd shouts you down.

options.label: Send the hero away a month

success.text: The crowd disperses.

stages.text: {heroName} paces the inn: too long in town, they say, and wants a fight.

success.text: The hero grins.

options.label: Give them the watch to drill

success.text: The watch is fitter.

stages.text: {heroName}'s old flame has arrived in town, married to a merchant.

success.text: Fireworks.
A polite dinner.

failure.text: A brawl in the inn.

stages.text: Every night a full mug at {tavern} is empty by morning, and the door's barred.

success.text: It's a game now.
The innkeeper's grandfather, sipping. He nods.

failure.text: You fall asleep.

stages.text: Travellers come to {tavern} to see the famous mug, and pay well for a pint.

success.text: Gold in the till, and some for the town.

stages.text: A stranger at {tavern} is winning every roll against the heroes. The heroes are reaching for swords.

success.text: Loaded. He runs.

failure.text: They're fair. He's lucky.

success.text: Before blood.

stages.text: Drinkers at {tavern} bet the mayor can't drink a yard of ale.

success.text: Down in one. Legend.

failure.text: Half of it down your front.

success.text: Booed, mildly.

stages.text: {tavern} has a new dark ale that makes men weep and sing.

success.text: Sold across three valleys.
A fine tax.

stages.text: The kitchen of {tavern} is on fire, and the cellar is full of brandy.

success.text: Out before the cellar.

failure.text: The brandy goes up. So does the tavern.

stages.text: Two bards at {tavern} are trying to out-sing each other, and it's been three days.

success.text: A tie. Everyone's hoarse.
Silence, golden.

stages.text: Twenty sellswords are drinking {tavern} dry and looking for work.

success.text: Twenty more swords.
They go, not quietly.

stages.text: A drunk at {tavern} sells maps to a ruin nobody's found, for a silver each.

success.text: Who knows?
He goes, still selling.

stages.text: A rider says a fever has emptied a village in the next valley.

success.text: Trade slows.
Brave. She comes back with knowledge.

stages.text: Three houses are down with the fever from the next valley.

success.text: It stops there.

failure.text: It spreads.

success.text: Prayer and broth.

stages.text: Plague doctors in beaked masks have come, asking for silver and the sick.

success.text: Leeches, vinegar, and some get better.
They know their trade. You keep the good ones.

failure.text: Charlatans.

stages.text: A month without a new grave. The fever has passed.

success.text: Bells and bread.
Names in stone.

stages.text: A dry cough is going round the lanes by {place}.

success.text: A dead dog in the cistern.

failure.text: It runs its course.

success.text: Soothed.

stages.text: A leper begs at the gate, and the guards want him gone.

options.label: Give him a hut and bread

success.text: The temple tends him.

options.label: Ask the clerics to heal him

success.text: Healed. He weeps.

failure.text: Beyond them.

stages.text: A sickness that kills in a day has struck {place}. Three dead by noon.

success.text: It burns out.

failure.text: More die.

success.text: It passes. The priests take credit.

stages.text: No rain since spring. The farmers are watching the sky.

success.text: Grumbling, but water.
Clear sky.

stages.text: The fields are cracking and the river's a trickle.

success.text: A ditch that saves half the crop.

failure.text: Dry ditch.

success.text: Dear.

stages.text: A rainmaker with drums and a goat says he'll bring rain for a fee.

success.text: Rain three days later. He was lucky. Or not.
A rain-calling at the old stones. Rain at dusk.

failure.text: No rain.

stages.text: Wolves have come down from the hills, and two sheep are dead.

success.text: Hunters go out.
Safer, hungrier.

stages.text: A wolf as big as a pony leads the pack now, and it looked into a child's window.

success.text: A grey pelt over the hall door.

failure.text: It hunts you.

success.text: The hero comes back with a story.

stages.text: Spring, and the wolves have gone back to the hills.

success.text: Lambs safe, folk merry.

stages.text: Hail like eggs flattened the barley by {place}.

success.text: Seed for replanting.
They mutter.

stages.text: Thick fog for a week. Carters lost, shops shut.

success.text: Carters find their way.

stages.text: Spring floods have left a sandbar of pearly shells by the landing.

success.text: Every house has a pearl.
Sold.

stages.text: Diggers by the river have found a skull as big as a cart.

success.text: A whole giant.
Let it rest.

stages.text: The scholars want the giant's bones set up in the town hall.

success.text: Folk come from all around.
A giant's grave.

stages.text: Three giants stand at the gate. They want their grandfather back.

success.text: Bones given with honour. The giants leave a gift.

failure.text: They take them, and the hall roof with them.

success.text: They nod and go.

stages.text: A stranger says he's the founder's great-grandson and wants the old founder's house.

success.text: They seem real.

failure.text: Can't tell.

success.text: He goes, swearing.

stages.text: The heir has a ring with the founder's mark. The old families are split.

options.label: Compare it with the founder's seal

success.text: A match. He's the heir.

failure.text: Forged. He's run out of town.

stages.text: The founder's heir wants a seat on the council by right of blood.

success.text: The old families are pleased.
The heir sulks, then runs for it.

stages.text: The false heir borrowed against the founder's house. Lenders want the town to pay.

success.text: The town's name is clean.
Lenders curse the town.

stages.text: A dying scholar left the town a box of books.

success.text: A shelf in the hall.
Gold.

stages.text: Folk are bringing books to the library: recipes, ledgers, a book of spells.

success.text: A useful book.

failure.text: It bites.

success.text: The library grows.

stages.text: Books are moved in the library at night, and a candle's lit.

success.text: The old scholar, still reading. You let him.

failure.text: It snuffs the candle.

stages.text: The library ghost leaves notes in the margins, correcting the scholars.

success.text: Scholars learn faster.

stages.text: A shepherd found a carved stone in the hills: a star chart, older than any kingdom.

success.text: An eclipse, due soon.

failure.text: It's a mystery.

stages.text: A retired clerk offers to teach the children to read, if the town gives him a room.

success.text: Children reading by winter.

stages.text: Renovating the old hall, workers found a map of tunnels under the town.

success.text: Old tunnels, sealed safe.

failure.text: Lost a lantern.

stages.text: With the gate shut, traders are stuck outside, shouting.

success.text: Trade.
Honest traders let in.

failure.text: A thief gets through.

stages.text: With the gate open, the town is full of strangers no one knows.

success.text: Safer.
Lively, risky.

stages.text: The gate vetters are letting in anyone with a silver.

success.text: Sacked.

failure.text: Can't prove it.

stages.text: A young watchman held a bridge alone against three robbers.

success.text: The watch is proud.

stages.text: The night watch was found drunk on duty, and the gate was open.

success.text: Lesson learned.
He's sober ever after.

stages.text: Lines at every bathhouse, every tavern, every temple.

success.text: Coming.
Orderly, if grumpy.

stages.text: Folk say the treasury is fat while they're thin.

success.text: Love.

options.label: Show them the walls it built

success.text: They understand.

failure.text: They don't.

stages.text: With the treasury low, a moneylender offers a loan at a tenth a month.

success.text: Gold now, pain later.
Lean times.

stages.text: Families without homes sleep in the square.

success.text: Warm.
They go to the fields.

stages.text: Bread is dear and a baker's window is smashed.

success.text: Bakers grumble.
Fed.

stages.text: A raven in the square says one word over and over: the mayor's name.

success.text: It says other names too.
A wizard's familiar. He apologises.

failure.text: It pecks you.

stages.text: A chest bought at the market bit off the buyer's finger.

success.text: A mimic. The scholars want it.

failure.text: It runs off on its lid.

stages.text: A ring of mushrooms has appeared overnight in the common.

success.text: Luck.
A wedding ring is lost the next day.

stages.text: The old standing stone outside town is weeping red water.

success.text: Iron in the rock and rain.

failure.text: An omen.

success.text: Calm.

stages.text: Frogs fell from the sky over the market.

success.text: Not bad.

stages.text: Children want the town cat made mayor. Some adults agree.

success.text: Ceremony.

stages.text: A small troll lives under the bridge and wants a toll of fish.

success.text: It guards the bridge.
It flees.

failure.text: It bites.

stages.text: A unicorn is eating apples in the orchard.

success.text: Blessing.
It vanishes, and the orchard rots.

stories.title: A ghost ship on the river

stages.text: A grey ship sails up the river at night, with no crew.

success.text: Lost souls, now rested.

failure.text: It sails on, and three men vanish.

stages.text: A great shadow passed over the town. A dragon, high up.

success.text: Everyone hides. It doesn't come back.
Nervous laughter.

stages.text: Builders found a jar of old coins in a wall.

success.text: Happy builders.
Gold.

stages.text: A swarm settled in the town hall chimney.

success.text: Honey for all.

stages.text: Children built a mud man by the river, and now it walks.

success.text: Back to mud.

failure.text: It walks into the river.

success.text: A tireless farmhand.

stages.text: A pigeon carries a golden ring and a note: 'Help'.

success.text: A trapped traveller, freed.

failure.text: Lost.

stages.text: A sword in the smithy hums when the north wind blows.

success.text: Old enchantment. Sold to a hero.

failure.text: It goes quiet.

stages.text: A gnome has set up a workshop and things explode daily.

success.text: A pump that works.

options.label: Move him to the edge of town

success.text: Explosions further off.

stages.text: Halfling traders want to hold a seven-meal feast.

success.text: Seven meals.

stages.text: A troop of dwarf masons offer their work for a year.

success.text: Stone like iron.

stages.text: An elf asks to plant a tree in the square.

success.text: A silver tree.

stages.text: An orc family wants to settle. Neighbours are wary.

success.text: Strong workers.
Accepted.

failure.text: They leave.

stages.text: A child born with horns, and the neighbours whisper.

success.text: Quiet.
Accepted.

failure.text: The family leaves.

stages.text: A goblin urchin is stealing from the market but feeding stray dogs.

success.text: A good errand-runner.
It goes.

stages.text: Kobolds have been found living in the quarry, offering to dig.

success.text: Fast diggers.
Gone.

stages.text: The ferryman is old and the ford is deep. The council talks of a stone bridge.

success.text: Masons measure the banks.
The ferryman is relieved.

stages.text: The ferryman says the bridge will starve him and his sons.

success.text: Tolls instead of oars.
He takes it, sour.

stages.text: The last stone is set. The whole town wants to walk across first.

success.text: A feast on the bridge.

options.label: Bless the stones against the river spirit

success.text: The river runs quiet under it.

failure.text: A stone falls in. The old folk shiver.

stages.text: Since the bridge was built, the river has taken a dog, a cart and nearly a child.

success.text: A silver ring thrown from the middle arch. The river is quiet.

failure.text: It takes the ring and a fisherman.

success.text: Sensible.

stages.text: A great lord writes that he'll pass through and stay three nights.

success.text: Rooms aired, the town scrubbed.
He'll take the town as it is.

stages.text: The lord rides in with forty men, sixty horses and a taste for venison.

success.text: He leaves praising the town at court.

failure.text: He finds the beds hard and says so at court.

success.text: He's pleased, and the larder's bare.

stages.text: The lord who stayed sends a cask of wine and a charter for a second market day.

success.text: Two market days.

stages.text: The lord who was slighted has raised the toll on the king's road through his lands.

success.text: The toll comes down, slowly.
Longer, cheaper.

stages.text: The council can never start on time: no two clocks in town agree.

success.text: Noon is noon.

stages.text: Every trader at {place} uses their own pound. The council wants one set of weights, in bronze, kept in the hall.

success.text: Fair trade.

stages.text: A baby was left on the hall steps with a note: 'for the town'.

success.text: Every house helps.
The priests take her in.

stages.text: The old wise woman who birthed half the town has died.

options.label: A funeral for the whole town

success.text: Everyone she delivered walks behind her.

stages.text: Hunters have brought down a boar as big as an ox.

success.text: Pork for everyone.

stages.text: Pilgrims bound for a far shrine ask to camp a night outside the walls.

success.text: They pray for the town.
A good market.

stages.text: The sweeps send small boys up the chimneys, and one is stuck.

success.text: Out black and crying.

failure.text: The chimney has to come down.

success.text: Brushes on poles.

stories.title: A music box in the hall

stages.text: A traveller left a music box that plays a tune nobody can forget.

success.text: Children dance to it.
Simple clockwork.

failure.text: It makes everyone sleepy.

decrees.name: Market tolls lifted
decrees.text: No tolls at the market. Stallholders come from further off, settlers follow them, and the treasury feels it.

decrees.name: A pension for the watch's widows
decrees.text: The town keeps the families of the watch it lost. Folk sleep easier for it.

decrees.name: The tavern curfew
decrees.text: The taps close at the evening bell. The lanes are quieter and the town is crosser.

decrees.name: Mended roads
decrees.text: Drained and gravelled roads: carts reach the building sites, and the road brings more hopefuls.

decrees.name: The eased tithe
decrees.text: The farms keep more of the harvest this season, and work the harder for it.

decrees.name: The guild's monopoly
decrees.text: One guild sets the prices in the ward. The treasury takes its share; nobody else likes it.

decrees.name: The levy
decrees.text: Every able hand drills on the green at dawn. The building sites stand half empty.

decrees.name: Merchants keep away
decrees.text: Word went round the trading houses that this town seizes grain. Caravans take the long road.

decrees.name: A quarter for the newcomers
decrees.text: The refugees have a quarter and a voice of their own, and their cousins are coming up the road.

decrees.name: Winter rationing
decrees.text: Every household draws a measured share from the common stores until the thaw.

decrees.name: Wards on the council chamber
decrees.text: Sigils on the lintels and bells that ring for no wind. A charm laid on a councillor is caught at the door.

A hedge-witch was given to the crowd.
The mayor stood between a hedge-witch and the crowd.
The mayor seized a merchant's hoard in the hungry winter.
The mayor made a paladin break their oath of mercy.
The town took a dark patron's gold.
The mayor's heroes talked raiders out of their hold instead of killing them.
Townsfolk carried off in a raid were never brought home.
Heroes brought home townsfolk carried off in a raid.
The mayor sent a hero packing.
The mayor forbade the town's heroes to take gifts from the dark powers.
The mayor let a stranger in a green coat sweeten the wells.
The mayor signed a smiling notary's contract without reading the small print.
The mayor took a crone's apples to cure the fever.
The town found households in its rolls that nobody remembers.
Heroes found the way down to what makes the town forget.
The town dealt with what made it forget its own.

The town sheltered goblin families the farmers wanted dead.
The town drove starving goblin families out into the hills.
The children of the lanes play at being the town's heroes.
A dowser found sweet water under the market, and the town dug for it.
The market well runs deep and cold, and the town drinks from it.
The town's first bell hangs in the square.
The bell rang cracked, and the founder swore to make it right.
The old scarecrow was left standing in the fields.
The old scarecrow was burned on the midsummer fire.
The millers swear something walks the mill at night.
The mill ghost was given a name and a place at table.
The town holds a chartered fair every summer.
The summer fair draws traders from three valleys.
The orchards were wassailed with cider and song.
The orchards went unwassailed.
The town buried its first dead in its own ground.
The road into town has a name of its own.
The town has a seal, cut in brass.
Someone forged the town seal.
A saint's finger bone came to the temple.
The town doubts its saint's finger bone.
The saint's finger bone worked a miracle in the square.
There's talk of a secret worship in the cellars.
The cellar worship has a name and a meeting place.
The cellar cult was broken.
The cellar cult was let go, watched.
A mage is building a tower at the edge of town.
The mage's tower blew its top off.
The tower mage is the town's own.
A wandering healer came to tend the sick.
The wandering healer stayed, and folk call her a saint.
A statue of the founder stands in the square.
The founder's statue was defaced.
Barrels go missing from the river landing, and nobody pays duty on them.
The town knows the smugglers' cellar.
The smugglers pay the town to look the other way.
The smugglers' ring was broken.
Someone has been casing the treasury.
The treasury was robbed.
A treasury robbery was foiled.
Some of the watch take bribes.
The watch was purged of its bribe-takers.
Two guilds are at each other's throats.
The guilds' feud was settled at the mayor's table.
Two great families of the town are feuding.
The feud came to a duel.
The feuding families were reconciled.
The refugees have a quarter of their own.
The refugees have a voice on the council.
Someone found letters that point at the council.
A councillor stood trial for treason.
Word came of a sickness in the next valley.
The sickness reached the town.
The town came through the sickness.
The rains failed this year.
The wells are low and the fields cracked.
Wolves came down from the hills in the hard winter.
A great grey wolf leads the pack.

The giant's bones lie in the town hall.
A stranger claims to be the founder's lost heir.
The founder's heir lives in the town.
The so-called heir was a fraud.
The tavern has a legend of its own.
The town has the start of a library.
A scholar's ghost haunts the library shelves.

The visiting lord left pleased.

callings.name: Warder of the chamber
callings.text: Keeps wards on the council chamber. A charm laid on a councillor is caught at the door.

callings.name: Truth-seer to the council
callings.text: Sits by the council door and hears every lie as a sour note. A foe's servant on the council is found out far sooner.

callings.name: The town's bard
callings.text: Plays the tavern every night. Spirits rise, and the road hears of it.

callings.name: Oath of the Shield
callings.text: Sworn to the walls. Stronger at the gate, steadier in the lanes.

callings.name: Oath of Mercy
callings.text: Sworn to the weak. The poor lanes are kinder, and the gods notice.

callings.name: Oath of Vengeance
callings.text: Sworn to hunt what preys on the town. Dread ebbs; the town is a grimmer place.

callings.name: Go-between to the Quiet Hand
callings.text: Sits at the thieves' table. Their knives stay off the town, and an envelope comes every week.

callings.name: Informer in the Quiet Hand
callings.text: Sits at the thieves' table and tells the watch. The guild grows hotter until it is exposed.

callings.name: Drillmaster of the militia
callings.text: Drills the militia at dawn. The walls are better held.

callings.name: Strongarm of the works
callings.text: Hauls beams and stone for the builders, for fun. Building goes faster.

callings.name: Preacher at the temple
callings.text: Preaches every rest day. The town's god is honoured and the lanes are calmer.

callings.name: Healer of the poor
callings.text: Tends the sick in the poorer lanes, with salves the town pays for.

callings.name: Keeper of the grove
callings.text: Keeps the old grove. Fields come up greener; less timber is cut.

callings.name: Woodward
callings.text: Chooses which trees fall. The woods and the fields both do better.

callings.name: Warden of the roads
callings.text: Walks the roads with a horn. Carters and settlers feel safer coming.

callings.name: Teacher of the dawn forms
callings.text: Teaches the forms at dawn. Apprentices are calmer and fight less.

callings.name: Trainer of the watch
callings.text: Trains the watch to fight with open hands. Steadier walls, fewer broken heads.

callings.name: Spark of the forges
callings.text: Lights the smiths' fires with wild magic. More tools, and the odd scorched roof.

callings.name: The patron's tithe
callings.text: Gold from the old well every week. Dread grows, and the gods turn away.

callings.name: The town's sage
callings.text: Runs a school of letters and numbers. Clerks are quicker and builders read plans.

callings.name: Warder of the walls
callings.text: Sets wards in the gatehouse stones. The walls are harder to breach.

callings.name: Keeper of the gate keys
callings.text: Holds the gate keys. Nothing comes in after dark unseen.

callings.name: Lantern of the outer wards
callings.text: Walks the lanes outside the walls at night. The newer wards sleep easier.

callings.name: Keeper of the map room
callings.text: Keeps the great map in the town hall. Settlers find their way here, and the wilds seem smaller.

callings.name: Keeper of the whispering relic
callings.text: Keeps a whispering relic at the temple. Pilgrims and the gods come closer; so does something else.

callings.name: The town's herbalist
callings.text: Brews salves and draughts by the apothecary fire. Fevers break sooner.

callings.name: Blesser of the fields
callings.text: Sings to the seed at dusk. The harvest comes up strong.
